newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Central America cries foul on Mexico sugar quotas.
newsitem.headline: Central America cries foul on Mexico sugar quotas.

text.p: Central American sugar producers here cried foul on Friday in the face of Mexico's attempts to boost its sugar quotas.

Regional economic ministers agreed to a joint battle against Mexico's efforts to boost its sugar exports to the United States. Mexico has only begun exporting recently after production exceeded domestic demand.

"If Mexico succeeds in this maneuvering and removes part of the Central American quota, we could lose sales to the United States of 30,000 tonnes," Central American Sugar Industry (AICA) executive director Jose Oribe told Reuters.

Mexico's Sugar Industry Chamber spokesman told Reuters in Mexico City it hoped to raise sugar cane exports from its limit of 25,000 tonnes per year to counter U.S. high fructose corn syrup imports of about 300,000 tonnes.
"When we signed the NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement), negotiators never thought that Mexico would have an excess supply of sugar," the spokesman said.
"We want to prevent high fructose corn syrup imports or make a more equal exchange between corn syrup and Mexico's sugar," he said.
Mexico is limited to 25,000 tonnes of exports to the United States until 2001, when the quota will be lifted to 100,000 tonnes. In 2010, the quota is scheduled to be removed.
Mexico and the United States are discussing possible adjustment of the quotas, the spokesman added.
"Mexico now wants a greater cut of sugar exports to the United States and has indicated that it does not recognize the validity of the accord," a Guatemalan official said.
He accused Mexico of looking to gain ground in the U.S. market at the expense of Central American exporters.

Central America exported in 1996 some 325,360 tonnes of sugar to the United States, he said, or 15 percent of all U.S. sugar imports. Mexico is prepared to boost exports to the market for the first time from its 1996-1997 harvest because it drew an exceptionally large crop.
